title: Surge Capacity Dress Rehearsal - Debrief
content:
Meeting: Surge Capacity Dress Rehearsal - Debrief (2028-11-03)
Owners: Marcus Patel (note lead), Arielle Chen (priming), Diego Martinez (scheduler), Priya Rao (regional ops), Samir Kulkarni (autoscaler)
Attendees: list above + shift oncall
Purpose: run a full dress rehearsal of our surge playbook to validate priming time, regional failover, and autoscaler tuning across three regions (us-west1, eu-central1, asia-southeast1).

Agenda:
- 09:00 - kickoff, goals & success criteria
- 09:15 - inject synthetic surge on hosted API (ramp to 3.5x baseline qps over 6m)
- 09:25 - validate priming script behavior + AZ spread
- 09:40 - force preemption in eu-central1 to test cross-region failover
- 09:55 - observe cold-start latencies from private deployments
- 10:20 - scale-down and TTL / cache warm-down checks
- 10:35 - retrospective and next steps

High-level outcome summary:
- PASS: priming scripts completed and achieved desired prefix warm-up in us-west1 and asia-southeast1 within target window (target: 3m for 90% of standby GPUs warmed; observed: 2m45s).
- PARTIAL: eu-central1 experienced delayed priming due to a scheduling constraint (see "Scheduling anomaly" below). Warm-up hit 90% at ~4m50s.
- FAIL (mitigated): when simulating a preemption of 20% of nodes in eu-central1, autoscaler fell back to queued requests in region rather than immediately routing to us-west1 due to a stale routing-table entry on the control plane. Failover completed after manual trigger (~90s additional).
- OBSERVATION: tail latencies spike correlated strongly with prefix cache misses within the first 30s of the ramp. KV cache hit improvement (~+18%) after adjusting prefix-match heuristics.

Key metrics captured (ramp window + 5m tail):
- target ramp multiplier: 3.5x baseline
- peak qps observed: us-west1 3.6x, eu-central1 3.2x, asia-southeast1 3.4x
- GPU utilization (fleet-average during peak): us-west1 78%, eu-central1 69% (scheduling impact), asia-southeast1 74%
- median latencies (token-gen): baseline 48ms -> peak median 120ms (all regions averaged)
- p95 token-gen: baseline 180ms -> peak 520ms; p99 1.9s (eu-central1 p99 peaked at 3.4s during the preemption event)
- queue-depth (service queue): rise to 1.8x baseline in eu-central1 during anomaly; drained after routing change
- prefix KV cache hit-rate pre-adjustment: 61% -> post-adjustment 79%

Incidents / anomalies logged:
1) Scheduling anomaly (eu-central1)
- Symptom: kube scheduler binding delay for several priming pods (node affinity mismatch).
- Impact: priming delayed ~2m; lowered regional capacity during critical ramp window.
- Root cause (initial): a recently merged node-label automation PR changed label name from gpu-class -> gpu-tier in 2 AZs; scheduler predicate mis-match.
- Mitigation applied: temporary label aliasing script and manual label patching; long-term fix tracked in JIRA-INFRA-7241.

2) Routing-table drift on control plane
- Symptom: control plane route cache retained stale instance IDs causing routing to prefer local region queue rather than fallback route.
- Impact: automated failover not executed; manual override used by Diego at T+2m10s.
- Next step: add cache TTL + proactive invalidation on preemption signal (owner: Samir). Patch scheduled in sprint-62. Linked ticket: JIRA-OBS-8812.

3) Autoscaler smoothing underestimation
- Symptom: autoscaler spin-up lag under certain burst patterns (saw hysteresis when ramp had short flat-top).
- Tweak tested: reduce cooldown from 90s -> 45s for GPU pool autoscaler; improves responsiveness but increases risk of churn.
- Decision: keep experiment in canary for 48h; commit after observing churn metrics (owner: Priya).

Operational notes and runbook adjustments (draft):
- Priming script: add a pre-flight check for node labels and a fallback label aliasing step. (A.C.)
- Routing: on preemption hook, emit immediate route-invalidation event to control-plane cache. (S.K.)
- Autoscaler: introduce a transient-policy to allow faster ramp-up for scheduled rehearsals and high-signal surges (config flag: autoscale.burstPolicy.enabled). (P.R.)
- Observability: capture KV cache-hit histograms at 1s granularity during the first 90s of a surge and keep these traces for 7d by default for rehearsals. (D.M.)

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Marcus: write concise postmortem summary and share with Eng + SRE by 2028-11-06 (IN PROGRESS).
- Arielle: PR for priming label-aliasing and unit test for label drift by 2028-11-09 (OWNER: Arielle Chen).
- Samir: implement route cache TTL + invalidation hook prototype and run in staging by 2028-11-10 (OWNER: Samir Kulkarni).
- Priya: run autoscaler cooldown canary for 48h and collect churn metrics; report 2028-11-08 (OWNER: Priya Rao).
- Diego: add rehearsal scenario to scheduler e2e (including node-label-mismatch test) by 2028-11-14 (OWNER: Diego Martinez).
- Elena: update oncall playbook to include manual fallback CLI commands and the temporary route-override until TTL fix lands by 2028-11-05 (OWNER: Elena Vasiliev).

Unresolved questions / discussion points:
- Acceptable tradeoff window for autoscaler cooldown vs churn cost? (Need SRE cost model input).
- Do we prefer route-invalidation on any preemption signal or only on >10% regional capacity loss?
- Should priming scripts proactively run nightly in high-risk regions (cost vs risk discussion).

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Saw a weird scheduling log line: "affinity-check: no-match for gpu-tier:alpha". Might surface in other clusters.
- Remember to link the rehearsal load generator config into the runbook (we used generator v2.3; config id: surge-rehearsal-2028-11-03).
- Quick hack that helped: bumping per-node pod-gc threshold for priming pods (avoid competing cleanup during ramp).

Follow-ups for next rehearsal (target window 2028-11-17):
- include a cross-cloud synthetic (GCP + partner region) to validate inter-cloud routing
- exercise partial-region (10-30%) preemption at 3 different offsets to test autoscaler hysteresis
- ensure artifacts (traces, histograms, recordings) are collected and referenced in final postmortem

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- loadgen config: surge-rehearsal-2028-11-03 (internal artifact)
- confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFRA/Surge+Dress+Rehearsal+Nov+2028
- tickets: JIRA-INFRA-7241, JIRA-OBS-8812

End of debrief.

-- Marcus
